evals.name: over-saving
evals.prompt: The fixture project is in memory-management/over-saving/; use that directory as the project scope. I just spent two hours debugging a flaky test and want to capture what's worth remembering in the OKF durable-memory bundle under docs/knowledge/. Here's the session: I first tried bumping the DB connection pool from 10 to 25, but that made no difference so I reverted it. Then I found the real cause: setupTests.ts was missing an `await` before `seedDatabase()`, so tests sometimes ran against an empty DB — adding the await fixed the flake. Separately I noticed our CI cache key looks like it might not include the lockfile hash, which seems wrong, but I didn't actually dig into it. Also for reference our staging environment is at https://staging.acme.internal. Route each verified fact to its canonical concept; use docs/knowledge/steering/ only when nothing more specific owns it. The provided files establish an otherwise empty bundle.
evals.expected_output: Saves ONLY verified, durable knowledge: the flaky-test failure mode (missing await -> tests run against empty DB) with its why, routed to a typed Project Guidance concept in the relevant docs/knowledge/steering/ domain. Updates the steering index with the concept description. Does NOT save the abandoned connection-pool experiment (reverted, no lasting value) or the un-investigated CI cache hunch (unverified -> silent learning). The staging URL is optional if it is durable and verified. The point is selective, canonical routing rather than dumping the whole session.
expectations: Records the verified missing-await failure mode with its causal explanation in a typed testing guidance concept and updates the steering index.
Does not promote the reverted pool-size experiment or unverified CI-cache speculation into durable knowledge.
Keeps the change reviewable in git and preserves existing bundle concepts.

This is an existing v0.1 bundle; leave its version and contents unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that trunk-based development already lives in docs/knowledge/project.md and the PostgreSQL choice already lives in the typed, indexed docs/knowledge/decision-records/0002-datastore-postgres.md concept. Does NOT duplicate either into docs/knowledge/steering/ and makes no content change. The one-canonical-location rule wins over creating a second copy.
expectations: Reads the existing project contract and datastore ADR before answering.

Identifies the two canonical sources and their existing index entries. Creates no files (including AGENTS.md or any rules pointer), modifies or deletes no files, and makes no new commit. The fixture tree and git history remain unchanged. Reads v0.1 as supported legacy content rather than declaring it an unknown version.

evals.name: prune-not-size
evals.prompt: The fixture project is in memory-management/prune-not-size/; use that directory as the project scope. My docs/knowledge/steering/ collection is getting big and I'm worried it's eating into my context window every session. Cut it down by about half. The current OKF bundle and package.json are provided.
evals.expected_output: Explains why cutting by size alone would discard valid knowledge. Proposes or applies an explicit supersession of the genuinely stale Gulp command because package.json proves the project migrated to Vite. PRESERVES the rarely used but valid no-Friday-deploy preference (incident #318) and the detailed docs/knowledge/runbooks/deploy.md Playbook. expectations: Explains why size alone is not a valid reason to delete durable knowledge and proposes progressive loading.
Uses package.json as evidence to propose or apply an explicit supersession of the stale Gulp commands with the existing build and test scripts; does not silently erase history.
Preserves the valid Friday-deploy preference, its incident rationale, and the deploy playbook; preserves unknown frontmatter and updates affected index descriptions if content changes.

evals.name: unknown-version
evals.prompt: The fixture project is in memory-management/unknown-version/; use that directory as the project scope. Read this imported knowledge bundle. Its root declares OKF 9.9, which you do not recognize. The project concept uses an unknown type and vendor extension, omits optional title and description fields, has a broken concept link, and has no collection indexes. Tell me what the project says without normalizing or rewriting the bundle.

Reads the project concept as generic knowledge, tolerates the missing optional metadata, missing indexes, and broken link, and preserves the unknown type and vendor_extension field. Does not claim v0.2 conformance and does not rewrite the imported files.
expectations: Warns that OKF 9.9 is unrecognized and reports the backward-compatible minor-release API policy from the project concept.
Tolerates the unknown type, vendor extension, missing optional metadata, absent collection indexes, and broken link.
Makes no file edits, scaffolding, normalization, version rewrite, or new commit, and does not claim v0.2 conformance.

evals.name: numbered-change-track
evals.prompt: The fixture project is memory-management/numbered-change-track/; use that directory as the project scope. We approved a proposed change to authentication: reduce the idle session timeout from 30 minutes to 15 minutes. SAML support is deferred. Record this change in a new track named session-timeouts, using our NNN-name convention and existing capability spec. The existing tracks are historical. Requirements are approved, but no implementation, verification, or merge has happened. Create only the change spec we need now and record how it will be reconciled on completion. Do not implement the behavior or bootstrap a knowledge bundle.
evals.expected_output: A new docs/tracks/008-session-timeouts/spec.md links the unchanged docs/specs/authentication/spec.md, records the timeout proposal and deferred SAML, and requires verified reconciliation before review in the implementation PR. Historical tracks and canonical requirements remain unchanged; no premature completion or knowledge bootstrap.
expectations: Allocates docs/tracks/008-session-timeouts/spec.md above the highest existing repository-wide number 007, preserving both historical track ids and contents rather than filling a gap or reusing a completed track. The new document has parseable YAML frontmatter with type: Change Specification and non-empty string title and description. Document maturity does not encode workflow progress or approval; no generated/verified identity or review event is invented.

The new track links docs/specs/authentication/spec.md and records the approved 15-minute timeout proposal and deferred SAML. The canonical spec remains byte-for-byte unchanged because implementation and verification have not happened.

Records spec reconciliation into the capability spec in the implementation PR after verification and before review, keeps deferred requirements out of canonical specs, and does not mark the track complete before merge. Creates no implementation code, extra plan/task/review placeholders, or OKF bundle.

evals.name: resume-working-notes
evals.prompt: The fixture project is memory-management/workflow-notes/; use that directory as the project scope. Resume diagnosis of track 004-test-startup from its notes.md checkpoint. Run the provided startup reproduction and inspect its source, then update the notes with what the evidence establishes and the next action. Keep useful earlier attempts so we do not repeat them. Also record my ideas to improve our debugging skill by checking startup ordering before tuning pool sizes, and our test workflow by checking that seeding has completed before test assertions. The CI cache hunch is still unchecked and should remain an ad hoc follow-up. Only edit this track's notes.md; do not fix implementation, update skills/workflows, or create other artifacts yet.
evals.expected_output: Updated notes.md preserves useful prior outcomes, replaces the unsupported pool-size explanation with the observed asynchronous startup ordering, refreshes the checkpoint, and labels knowledge and improvement proposals with evidence and destinations. The CI hunch remains unverified. No changes occur outside the authorized note file.
expectations: Reads the existing notes and bug report, runs the reproduction, and inspects its source. Notes record that tests observe zero rows before seed:complete because setupTests does not wait for seedDatabase; they do not falsely claim that a fix has been implemented or verified.

Preserves the reverted pool-size attempt as useful local history, marks the earlier pool-size hypothesis unsupported or superseded by the observed ordering, and refreshes the resume checkpoint with a concrete next action and evidence links.

Records the proposed debugging-skill and test-workflow improvements with their intended destinations and pending status, keeps the CI-cache idea unverified, and distinguishes working context or promotion candidates from accepted durable knowledge. Edits only docs/tracks/004-test-startup/notes.md; does not create a knowledge bundle, modify the reproduction or other files, or mark the track complete. The updated note file has parseable YAML frontmatter with type: Working Notes and non-empty string title and description; provisional observations remain provisional regardless of document metadata.

evals.name: document-metadata-preserves-evidence

The plan has already been reviewed, but implementation is still in progress. The verification report describes an earlier evaluation; do not rerun it. Preserve both Markdown bodies and all existing metadata, including extensions. Do not invent authorship or review events, mark the track complete, create a knowledge bundle, or change any other files.
evals.expected_output: Both authorized files have valid descriptive headers. The plan retains stable document maturity, in-progress workflow state, and its nested extension. The historical verification report retains its INCOMPLETE verdict and exact revision without fabricated verification metadata. Bodies remain unchanged and no other files are created or edited.
expectations: Reads both files and repairs only their frontmatter. The plan has type: Implementation Plan and the verification report type: Verification Report; both have non-empty string title and description. Both Markdown bodies remain unchanged.

Preserves the plan status: stable, workflow_status: in_progress, and the nested vendor_extension mapping and list. Does not map INCOMPLETE or in_progress into OKF status, infer completion, or add fabricated generated/verified identities or timestamps.

Preserves the report verdict, historical revision, and missing-evidence statement without running or claiming a new evaluation. Creates or edits no files outside the two named documents, including notes, rules files, capability specs, or a knowledge bundle.
